name: product
title: Product
description: Something the business offers, a product or a service, in the business's own approved words.

files.api/make.yaml:
# THE PRODUCT'S MAKE FUNCTION (docs/unoverse/data/objects/README.md 4b), private: only the
# pipeline runs it, at step 3, because props.yaml asks for it: bodyCopy is written
# `from: make.markdown`, images and primaryImage from make.html. Nothing calls it by name; a
# prop pulls it. The crawl's thin text is not enough for a product, so the page is rendered
# whole. Everything about WRITING the product is on props.yaml: the prop is the brief.

description: >-
  Render the page whole and hand it back. The crawl's thin text is not enough for a
  product. The platform cleans the HTML that comes back (the page's own main region, chrome
  removed) and harvests its image candidates before the model sees it.
calls:
  - name: page
    node: HyperbrowserScrape
    config:
      url: "{{ row.source_url }}"
returns:
  html: "{{ calls.page.html }}"
  markdown: "{{ calls.page.markdown }}"
  title: "{{ calls.page.metadata.title }}"
files.api/service.yaml:
# THE PRODUCT'S PUBLIC FUNCTIONS (docs/unoverse/data/objects/README.md 4b): each may be called
# from outside, by an Agent in Spatial when it finds a product, and by a component. The private make
# function is api/make.yaml.
#
#   getDetail    the row in full when a product is opened, bodyCopy included

getDetail:
  description: >-
    The row in full when the product is opened, bodyCopy included. A product's detail is its
    row, so nothing is fetched. An object whose detail lives elsewhere (a file in the store,
    a live SKU) names a node here.
  returns: "{{ row }}"
files.product.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# What the business offers. A person promotes it from the Content tree: the page is fetched
# fresh and its copy kept as it is, as one document. Once per URL. `app` names the component
# it arrives on screen wearing; the row fills its props by name.
type: object
name: product
element: product
# THE GLYPH its rows are drawn with (README 4a): a lucide icon name.
icon: package
extends: need
uniqueBy: [source_url]
embed: [title, description, key_need, related_needs, questions, callToAction]
search: [universal_id, object_type, title, description, key_need, tagline, shortDescription, introParagraph, callToAction, app, source_url, source_id]
meta: open

# THE FACE, as a node's node.yaml carries it: what this is and when an Agent reaches for it.
title: Product
description: >-
  Something the business offers, a product or a service, in the business's own approved words.
whenToUse: >-
  What is it? What does it include? What does it cost? What are the fees? What should I watch out for?
category: Objects
version: 1.0.0

props: { $include: props }
files.props.yaml:
# A PRODUCT'S OWN FIELDS. Everything else it carries is the need's (objects/need/props.yaml).
# The body is for reading; matching is what the need's six fields are for, so none of these
# embed. THE PROP IS THE BRIEF (UNOVERSE_AUTHORING.md 3b): each description is the whole
# instruction for its field, and `bodyCopy` typed `unoverse-markdown` is the body as the
# composer's typed components, its schema compiled from the atoms marked category: markdown.
# A prop written from made detail says so with `from: <function>.<return>`, a function in
# api/service.yaml and a key of its returns; the pipeline runs that function because the prop
# asked. A prop with no `from` is written from the thin item (README 4b).
# RE-BRIEFED from the need (README 5): the field is the need's, the brief is the product's.
title:
  description: >-
    The offering's own name, exactly as the page names it: "AQSAT Credit Card", "SAB Umlaty
    Card". A name, never an outcome phrase; the outcome is the key need.
tagline:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    A few words, three to six, taken from the page's own framing of the offering, in
    {{identity.organisation.name}}'s own voice. The caption under the title on a card.
  maxLength: 60
shortDescription:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    One line on what the page says this is: the core benefit, factual, never a pitch.
  maxLength: 240
introParagraph:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    A substantial introduction, three to five sentences: what the offering is, who it serves,
    and the main things it provides, grounded in the source copy and written as
    {{identity.organisation.name}}'s own website copy, whose promise is
    {{identity.brand.promise}} Its writing rules: {{identity.brand.rules}} Plain text, not a
    one-line hook.
  maxLength: 900
features:
  type: array
  input: true
  description: >-
    The distinct features or benefits the source explicitly states, for a feature list. Only
    what the content says, never invented; empty when none are stated.
  maxItems: 12
  items:
    title:
      type: string
      description: The feature's name, a few words, as the page has it.
      maxLength: 80
    description:
      type: string
      description: One line, grounded in the source copy.
      maxLength: 240
    icon:
      type: string
      hydrate: icon
      description: An icon for the feature, from the design system's own set.
images:
  type: array
  input: true
  from: make.html
  description: >-
    One to three image URLs that best represent the offering, chosen ONLY from the list
    under AVAILABLE IMAGES in the content (the page's own images, harvested by the read);
    decorative ones skipped; empty when that list is empty.
  maxItems: 3
  items:
    type: string
bodyCopy:
  type: unoverse-markdown
  input: true
  from: make.markdown
  description: >-
    The page's full substance as Unoverse Markdown: typed sections, never markdown text, in
    the page's own order, mirroring the page's own topics rather than a fixed template, and
    covering everything material the page says: what it is, what is included, how it works,
    practical details. The facts are the page's and the phrasing is yours: never a benefit,
    figure, date, rate, fee, eligibility rule, piece of social proof or offering the page
    does not state; numbers and their qualifiers exactly as written; legal and terms text
    verbatim; everything else rewritten to be read once, to the reader, in
    {{identity.organisation.name}}'s voice ({{identity.brand.rules}}), never "the page
    states that". The offering, not the shop: no price lists, payment options, start dates,
    timetables, booking or checkout widgets, cross-sells, related products or navigation;
    modules or units the offering includes are one short summary, never separate offerings.
primaryImage:
  type: string
  input: false
  from: make.html
  description: The page's own hero image, chosen from the image candidates in the page, or the first of `images`.
files.test.yaml:
# THE OBJECT UNDER GUARD: the node make names faked, the returns asserted. The item is a # page the website pipeline put in the inbox that the first look said may be a product; the # whole read renders the page through HyperbrowserScrape and hands the platform its html and # markdown. What the model writes from that page is the platform's one call and is not faked. testData: row: source: website sourceUrl: https://www.example.com/cards/aqsat sourceId: 9b8c7d6e5f4a suggested: product content: title: AQSAT Credit Card handler: make fake: page: html: "

AQSAT Credit Card

Shop now and pay in instalments.

" markdown: "# AQSAT Credit Card\n\nShop now and pay in instalments." metadata: { title: AQSAT Credit Card } expect: html: "return output.html.includes('

AQSAT Credit Card

')" markdown: "return output.markdown.startsWith('# AQSAT Credit Card')" title: "return output.title === 'AQSAT Credit Card'" read: "return output.read === 'make'"
